q: Freyssinet's Plougastel Bridge (1930) was notable at its completion for being what?
o: The first bridge made of prestressed steel
The largest reinforced-concrete bridge, with three 187-meter spans
The tallest bridge in the world
The first suspension bridge in Europe
n: At its completion, the Plougastel Bridge (1930) was the largest reinforced-concrete bridge, with three spans of 187 meters each. (Source: Famous Architects, #12 Eugène Freyssinet)

q: Charles Rennie Mackintosh (1868–1928) was a prominent figure in which movement/style?
o: Arts and Crafts and Art Nouveau
n: The Scottish architect and designer Mackintosh was a prominent figure in the Arts and Crafts movement and Art Nouveau style. (Source: Famous Architects, #7 Charles Rennie Mackintosh)

q: Which architect said, "Seek truth in beauty, and beauty in truth"?
n: This dictum, along with "Architecture must be rooted in place and culture," belongs to Moshe Safdie (b. 1938). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #35 Moshe Safdie)

q: Inigo Jones (1573–1652) introduced classical architecture to Britain, influenced by the Italian Renaissance and the works of which architect?
n: Jones, an English architect who introduced classical architecture to Britain, was influenced by the Italian Renaissance and the works of Palladio. (Source: Famous Architects, #20 Inigo Jones)

q: Which architect said, "I don't divide architecture, landscape and gardening; to me they are one"?
n: This dictum, and "Any architectural work that does not express serenity is an error," belong to Louis Barragán (1902–1988). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #31 Louis Barragán)

q: Eero Saarinen (1910–1961), known for dynamic curves suggesting movement and flight, was the son of which fellow architect?
n: Eero Saarinen was a Finnish American architect and son of Eliel Saarinen, known for innovative sculptural designs like the TWA Flight Center and the Gateway Arch. (Source: Famous Architects, #9 Eero Saarinen)

q: Kenzo Tange (1913–2005) played a pivotal role in post-war reconstruction and urban planning in which country?
n: Tange, a Japanese architect who fused traditional Japanese styles with modernism, played a pivotal role in post-war reconstruction and urban planning in Japan, reflecting the influence of Le Corbusier. (Source: Famous Architects, #24 Kenzo Tange)

q: Which architect/designer said, "The details are not the details. They make the design"?
n: "The details are not the details. They make the design" is a dictum of Charles Eames (1907–1978). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #25 Charles Eames)

q: The Triumvirate of Modern Philippine Architecture consists of Juan Nakpil, Pablo Antonio, and which other architect?
n: The Triumvirate of Modern Philippine Architecture consists of Juan Nakpil, Pablo Antonio, and Leandro Locsin. (Source: Architectural Groups (Local), #4 The Triumvirate of Modern Philippine Architecture)

q: William Van Alen (1883–1954), an American architect, is best known for designing which Art Deco skyscraper in New York City?
n: Van Alen's work epitomizes the Art Deco style with its ornate detailing and spire, best known for designing the Chrysler Building in New York City. (Source: Famous Architects, #53 William Van Alen)

q: Which architect described the architect as "not only the director, but... the composer"?
n: This dictum, along with "Architecture and sculpture are two rivers in which the same water flows," belongs to Santiago Calatrava (b. 1951). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #20 Santiago Calatrava)

q: Which architect said, "Buildings should be good neighbors"?
n: "Buildings should be good neighbors" is a dictum of Cesar Pelli (1926–2019). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #26 Cesar Pelli)

q: Which architect is famous for the dictum "Form follows function"?
n: "Form follows function" is a famous dictum of Louis Sullivan (1856–1924). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #1 Louis Sullivan)

q: Peter Behrens (1868–1940) was a pioneer of modern industrial design and played a significant role in developing what business concept?
n: The German architect and designer Behrens was a pioneer of modern industrial design and played a significant role in the development of corporate identity, as with the AEG Turbine Factory. (Source: Famous Architects, #38 Peter Behrens)

q: Which of the following was NOT one of the Bauhaus's directors?
n: The Bauhaus's directors were Walter Gropius, Hannes Meyer, and Ludwig Mies van der Rohe. Marcel Breuer was a Master Teacher (Furniture), not a director. (Source: Architectural Groups (International), #1 The Bauhaus)

q: James Stirling (1926–1992), a British architect known for bold modernist designs, is known for the Engineering Building at which university?
n: Stirling's Engineering Building at the University of Leicester (1963) was recognized for its innovative use of space and materials, marking a departure from traditional academic architecture. (Source: Famous Architects, #21 James Stirling)

q: Juan F. Nakpil (National Artist, 1973) was regarded as the 'Dean of Filipino Architects' and was:
o: The designer of the Chrysler Building
The first National Artist for Architecture
n: Juan F. Nakpil was regarded as the 'Dean of Filipino Architects' and was the first National Artist for Architecture, championing a distinctly Filipino architecture. (Source: National Artist for Architecture, #1 Juan F. Nakpil)

q: Which architect said, "Architecture begins where engineering ends"?
n: "Architecture begins where engineering ends" and "Art and technology—a new unity" are dicta of Walter Gropius (1883–1969). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #7 Walter Gropius)

q: Daniel Burnham (1846–1912) was a leading figure in which urban planning movement?
n: Burnham was a leading figure in the City Beautiful movement, promoting beautification and monumental grandeur in urban planning, notably through the Plan of Chicago (1909). (Source: Famous Architects, #6 Daniel Burnham)

q: Which architect said, "Beauty is the harmony of purpose and form"?
n: "Beauty is the harmony of purpose and form" is a dictum of Alvar Aalto (1898–1976). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #9 Alvar Aalto)

q: Which architect asked, "There are 360 degrees. Why stick to one?"
n: "There are 360 degrees. Why stick to one?" is a dictum of Zaha Hadid (1950–2016). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #14 Zaha Hadid)

q: Alvar Aalto (1898–1976) is known for a humanistic approach to modernism that integrates which elements?
n: The Finnish architect and designer Aalto is known for his humanistic approach to modernism, integrating natural materials and organic forms across architecture, furniture, and glassware design. (Source: Famous Architects, #3 Alvar Aalto)

q: Francisco Mañosa spent his career refining the Bahay Kubo and which other traditional Filipino house type into modern structures?
n: Mañosa spent his career refining the Bahay Kubo and Bahay na Bato into modern structures, championing indigenous materials like bamboo, rattan, coconut, and capiz shells. (Source: National Artist for Architecture, #6 Francisco "Bobby" Mañosa)

q: Which architect said, "Architecture is a way of seeing, thinking, and questioning our world and our place in it"?
n: This dictum belongs to Thom Mayne (b. 1944). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #28 Thom Mayne)

q: The Deconstructivists were architects featured in a seminal 1988 exhibition at which institution?
n: The Deconstructivists were the only architects featured in the seminal 1988 MoMA exhibition 'Deconstructivist Architecture,' curated by Philip Johnson and Mark Wigley. (Source: Architectural Groups (International), #5 The Deconstructivists)

q: Which architect said, "A house is like a flowerpot"?
n: "A house is like a flowerpot" and "A building can be designed only when the designer knows exactly how it will be used" are dicta of Richard Neutra (1892–1970). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #38 Richard Neutra)

q: Francisco 'Bobby' Mañosa (National Artist, 2018) was the most vocal advocate for which architectural approach?
n: Mañosa was the most vocal advocate for Neo-vernacular architecture, famously stating 'I design Filipino, nothing else.' (Source: National Artist for Architecture, #6 Francisco "Bobby" Mañosa)

q: Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM), an American firm founded in 1936, is renowned for contributions to modernist architecture and skyscraper design. Which of these is a SOM project?
n: SOM's notable works include Willis Tower (formerly Sears Tower), Burj Khalifa (the tallest structure globally, with SOM as lead architect), and One World Trade Center. (Source: Famous Architects, #50 Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM))

q: Which major complex, remaining a masterclass in Brutalist architecture, did Leandro Locsin design?
o: The National Library of the Philippines
n: Locsin designed the iconic Cultural Center of the Philippines (CCP) complex, which remains a masterclass in Brutalist architecture. (Source: National Artist for Architecture, #3 Leandro V. Locsin)

q: Joseph Paxton (1803–1865) is best known for designing the Crystal Palace, a pioneering example of prefabricated iron and glass architecture built for which event?
n: Paxton, an English gardener, architect, and engineer, designed the Crystal Palace, a pioneering example of prefabricated iron and glass architecture, built for the Great Exhibition of 1851. (Source: Famous Architects, #23 Joseph Paxton)

q: Which architect said, "The city is an addictive machine from which there is no escape"?
n: "The city is an addictive machine from which there is no escape" and "Form follows performance" are dicta of Rem Koolhaas (b. 1944). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #12 Rem Koolhaas)

q: Which architect served as professor and mentor to many of the core Metabolist Group members, using his international prestige to give them a platform?
n: Kenzo Tange was the professor and mentor to many of the core Metabolist members, using his international prestige to give the younger Metabolists a platform at the World Stage 1960. (Source: Architectural Groups (International), #2 The Metabolist Group)

q: Which building was Antoni Gaudí's first major commission, designed in a Gothic Revival style?
n: Gaudí designed his first major commission, Casa Vincens in Barcelona, using a Gothic Revival style that set a precedent for his future works. (Source: Famous Architects, #4 Antoni Gaudí)

q: Zaha Hadid's Guangzhou Opera House, known as the 'double pebble,' was inspired by what?
n: The Guangzhou Opera House, known as the 'double pebble,' was inspired by river stones smoothed by erosion. (Source: Famous Architects, #53(Zaha Hadid))

q: Which architect/planner said, "Make no little plans; they have no magic to stir men's blood"?
n: "Make no little plans; they have no magic to stir men's blood" and "Make big plans; aim high in hope and work..." are dicta of Daniel Burnham (1846–1912). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #41 Daniel Burnham)

q: Which architect said, "Architecture is the art of how to waste space"?
n: "Architecture is the art of how to waste space" and "All architects want to live beyond their deaths" are dicta of Philip Johnson (1906–2005). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #10 Philip Johnson)

q: Which of these is a notable work of National Artist Francisco 'Bobby' Mañosa?
n: Mañosa's notable works include The Coconut Palace ('Tahanang Pilipino'), Pasay City, showcasing the versatility of the coconut tree, as well as the EDSA Shrine and Amanpulo Resort. (Source: National Artist for Architecture, #6 Francisco "Bobby" Mañosa)

q: Which pensionado, the youngest of the group, designed the Manila City Hall and the Agriculture and Finance Building?
n: Antonio Toledo, the youngest pensionado, designed the Manila City Hall and the Agriculture and Finance Building. (Source: Architectural Groups (Local), #1 The Pensionados)

q: Robert Venturi (1925–2018), a leading figure in the postmodern movement, challenged modernist principles by advocating for what in architecture?
n: Venturi challenged modernist principles, advocating for 'complexity and contradiction' in architecture, as seen in the Vanna Venturi House. (Source: Famous Architects, #47 Robert Venturi)

q: Which architect said, "Always design a thing by considering it in its next larger context—a chair in a room, a room in a house, a house in an environment"?
n: This dictum belongs to Eero Saarinen (1910–1961). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #37 Eero Saarinen)

q: Adolf Loos (1870–1933) is best known for which influential essay advocating the elimination of unnecessary ornamentation?
n: Loos's essay 'Ornament and Crime' argued that removing ornament was a sign of cultural evolution, and emphasized functionality and simplicity. (Source: Famous Architects, #1 Adolf Loos)

q: Which architect said, "Each new situation requires a new architecture"?
n: "Each new situation requires a new architecture" is a dictum of Jean Nouvel (b. 1945). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #22 Jean Nouvel)

q: Jose Maria Zaragoza's Sto. Domingo Church, a National Cultural Treasure, is a fusion of Spanish Colonial 'Mission style' and which other style?
n: Sto. Domingo Church, Quezon City—arguably Zaragoza's most famous work and a declared National Cultural Treasure—is a fusion of Spanish Colonial 'Mission style' and Modernism. (Source: National Artist for Architecture, #5 Jose Maria Zaragoza)

q: Which architect said, "Form follows beauty" and "Architecture is invention"?
n: "Form follows beauty" and "Architecture is invention" are dicta of Oscar Niemeyer (1907–2012). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #18 Oscar Niemeyer)

q: Which building exemplifies Adolf Loos's minimalist aesthetic and rationalist design principles?
n: The Steiner House in Vienna, Austria, exemplifies Loos's minimalist aesthetic and rationalist design principles. (Source: Famous Architects, #1 Adolf Loos)

q: Le Corbusier (1887–1965), born Charles Édouard Jeanneret-Gris, was a Swiss French architect known as a pioneer of modern architecture. Which of these is his notable work?
n: Le Corbusier's notable works include Villa Savoye, France; Unité d'Habitation, Marseille; Notre-Dame du Haut, Ronchamp; and Chandigarh, India. (Source: Famous Architects, #26 Le Corbusier)

q: Deshamanya Geoffrey Bawa (1919–2003) is widely revered as the 'Father of' which architectural movement?
n: Bawa is widely revered as the 'Father of Tropical Modernism,' proving that Modernist principles could be adapted to the tropical, humid, culturally rich context of South and Southeast Asia. (Source: Famous Architects, #8 Deshamanya Geoffrey Bawa)

q: The Pioneer Triumvirate refers to the three men credited with establishing the foundations of the architecture profession in the Philippines in the early 20th century. Who were they?
o: Carlos Barretto, Antonio Toledo, and Tomas Mapua
Jose Maria Zaragoza, Carlos Arguelles, and Edmundo Lucero
Juan Nakpil, Tomas Mapua, and Juan Arellano
Juan Nakpil, Pablo Antonio, and Leandro Locsin
n: The Pioneer Triumvirate—Juan Nakpil, Tomas Mapua, and Juan Arellano—are credited with establishing the foundations of the profession in the early 20th century. (Source: Architectural Groups (Local), #3 The Pioneer Triumvirate)

q: Zaha Hadid (1950–2016), an Iraqi British architect often called the 'Queen of the Curve,' made history in 2004 by becoming:
o: The first woman to win the Pritzker Architecture Prize
The first woman to lead the Bauhaus
The first woman inducted into the AIA
The first woman to design a skyscraper in New York
n: In 2004, Zaha Hadid became the first woman to win the Pritzker Architecture Prize. (Source: Famous Architects, #53(Zaha Hadid))

q: Which architect said, "A house is a machine for living in"?
n: "A house is a machine for living in" is one of Le Corbusier's (1887–1965) famous dicta. (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #3 Le Corbusier)

q: Frank Gehry (b. 1929) revolutionized architecture by using which aerospace software to design buildings with unconventional, sculptural forms?
n: As a leader of Deconstructivism, Gehry revolutionized the field by using aerospace software (CATIA) to design buildings that look like they are in motion. (Source: Famous Architects, #13 Frank Gehry)

q: Which architect said, "If you want an easy life, don't be an architect"?
n: "If you want an easy life, don't be an architect" and "Architecture is really about well-being" are dicta of Renzo Piano (b. 1937). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #15 Renzo Piano)

q: Which campus, considered the largest collection of Art Deco structures in Manila, was designed by National Artist Pablo S. Antonio?
n: The Far Eastern University (FEU) Campus, Manila, designed by Pablo S. Antonio, is considered the largest collection of Art Deco structures in Manila, featuring Nicanor Reyes Hall, the Engineering building, and the Administration building. (Source: National Artist for Architecture, #2 Pablo S. Antonio)

q: Which architect said, "There is a powerful need for symbolism, and that means the architecture must have something that appeals to the human heart"?
n: This dictum, along with "The city must be subject to growth, decay and renewal," belongs to Kenzo Tange (1913–2005). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #30 Kenzo Tange)

q: Zaha Hadid pioneered which design approach alongside her partner Patrik Schumacher?
n: Alongside her partner Patrik Schumacher, Hadid pioneered Parametricism, pushing the construction industry to develop new methods for curved concrete and non-linear geometries. (Source: Famous Architects, #53(Zaha Hadid))

q: Which architect said, "Architecture is always political"?
n: "Architecture is always political" and "Form follows profit is the aesthetic principle of our times" are dicta of Richard Rogers (1933–2021). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #19 Richard Rogers)

q: Aldo Rossi's seminal book 'L'architettura della città' (The Architecture of the City) emphasizes which idea?
o: The importance of ornament in design
The elimination of all historical references
The importance of historical continuity in urban planning
n: Rossi's book emphasizes the importance of historical continuity in urban planning, tied to his concept of 'Collective Memory'—that urban form preserves the history and identity of its citizens. (Source: Famous Architects, #2 Aldo Rossi)

q: Leandro Locsin's Church of the Holy Sacrifice at UP Diliman was notable as the first Catholic church in the Philippines to feature:
o: A circular design and a thin-shell concrete dome
A bell tower in the Baroque style
n: The Church of the Holy Sacrifice, UP Diliman, is the first Catholic church in the country with a circular design and a thin-shell concrete dome. (Source: National Artist for Architecture, #3 Leandro V. Locsin)

q: Which architect/designer said, "To create, one must first question everything"?
n: This dictum belongs to Eileen Gray (1878–1976). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #39 Eileen Gray)

q: Antoni Gaudí pioneered the use of which structural technique to create self-supporting structures without traditional flying buttresses?
n: Gaudí pioneered the use of the catenary arch—an upside-down hanging chain model—to create self-supporting structures without the need for traditional flying buttresses. (Source: Famous Architects, #4 Antoni Gaudí)

q: Which architect, responding to Mies van der Rohe, argued "Less is a bore"?
n: "Less is a bore" and "More is More" are famous dicta of Robert Venturi (1925–2018). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #6 Robert Venturi)

q: Which Deconstructivist architect is known for the Parc de la Villette project?
n: Bernard Tschumi is known for the Parc de la Villette project among the Deconstructivists. (Source: Architectural Groups (International), #5 The Deconstructivists)

q: Which architect said, "Architecture has its own realm. It has a special physical relationship with life"?
n: This dictum belongs to Peter Zumthor (b. 1943). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #23 Peter Zumthor)

q: I.M. Pei (1917–2019), a Chinese-American architect known for modernist designs, is famous for designing which glass structure at a major museum in Paris?
n: I.M. Pei's Louvre Pyramid (1989) is a glass and metal pyramid serving as the main entrance to the Louvre Museum, blending contemporary design with its historic surroundings. (Source: Famous Architects, #19 I.M. Pei)

q: Michael Graves (1934–2015), a prominent postmodernist, designed over 2,000 household items including which famous item?
o: The Alessi teakettle with a bird-shaped whistle
n: Graves designed over 2,000 household items, including the iconic Alessi teakettle with a bird-shaped whistle, and integrated classical elements with modern design, whimsy, and color. (Source: Famous Architects, #32 Michael Graves)

q: Which architect said, "Architecture is not based on concrete and steel, and the elements of the soil. It's based on wonder"?
n: This dictum belongs to Daniel Libeskind (b. 1946). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #16 Daniel Libeskind)

q: Pier Luigi Nervi (1891–1979), an Italian engineer and architect, was renowned for combining engineering precision with architectural elegance using which material?
n: Nervi was renowned for his innovative use of reinforced concrete, combining engineering precision with architectural elegance, and often featured thin-shell structures. (Source: Famous Architects, #42 Pier Luigi Nervi)

q: Which Filipino National Artist stated that "buildings should be planned with austerity in mind... simple in design but dignified, true to a purpose"?
n: This dictum belongs to Pablo Antonio (1901–1975). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #40 Pablo Antonio)

q: Which architect said, "An architect does not need to spend his whole career making monuments for rich people"?
n: This dictum belongs to Shigeru Ban (b. 1957). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #36 Shigeru Ban)

q: Which architect at SOM pushed the firm toward a new level of architectural recognition in 1952 with the design for the Lever House?
n: In 1952, Gordon Bunshaft pushed SOM toward a new level of architectural recognition with his design for the Lever House, a curtain-walled office block in the international style. (Source: Famous Architects, #50 Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM))

q: Louis Kahn (1901–1974) is known for monumental and monolithic designs characterized by his use of which elements?
n: Kahn's work is characterized by its use of natural light and geometric forms, as seen in the Salk Institute for Biological Studies and the Kimbell Art Museum. (Source: Famous Architects, #28 Louis Kahn)

q: Jose Maria Zaragoza (National Artist, 2014) was the master of which architectural specialty, defining the modern Catholic aesthetic in the Philippines?
n: Zaragoza was the master of Ecclesiastical Architecture, defining the modern Catholic aesthetic in the Philippines during the mid-20th century. (Source: National Artist for Architecture, #5 Jose Maria Zaragoza)

q: Eugène Freyssinet (1879–1962) is celebrated as the father of which construction innovation?
n: The French structural engineer Freyssinet is celebrated as the father of prestressed concrete, revolutionizing the use of concrete for longer spans and more daring forms. (Source: Famous Architects, #12 Eugène Freyssinet)

q: Victor Horta (1861–1947), a Belgian architect and pioneer of the Art Nouveau movement, designed which building considered the first true Art Nouveau building?
n: Horta's Hôtel Tassel, Brussels, is considered the first true Art Nouveau building. (Source: Famous Architects, #51 Victor Horta)

q: Which architect said, "A room is not a room without natural light" and "Even a brick wants to be something"?
n: "A room is not a room without natural light" and "Even a brick wants to be something" are dicta of Louis Kahn (1901–1974). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #11 Louis Kahn)

q: Santiago Calatrava (b. 1951), known for sculptural and dynamic structures inspired by natural forms and human anatomy, rarely designed which kind of building?
n: Calatrava rarely designed a total enclosed building; most of his creations, like the Turning Torso and City of Arts and Sciences, are open structures. (Source: Famous Architects, #48 Santiago Calatrava)

q: Which architect declared, "Ornament is crime"?
n: "Ornament is crime" is the famous dictum of Adolf Loos (1870–1933). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #2 Adolf Loos)

q: Which Frank Lloyd Wright house was built over a waterfall in Pennsylvania in 1935?
n: Fallingwater (1935) is a house in Pennsylvania built over a waterfall, exemplifying Wright's philosophy of integrating architecture with nature. (Source: Famous Architects, #14 Frank Lloyd Wright)

q: Helmut Jahn (1940–2021) was known for combining which two design sensibilities in his bold buildings?
n: The German American architect Jahn was known for his high-tech and postmodern designs, such as the James R. Thompson Center (1985) in Chicago. (Source: Famous Architects, #18 Helmut Jahn)

q: The Manila Carnival Architects are referred to in architectural history as the designers of elaborate pavilions and structures for the Manila Carnival, held during which years?
n: The Manila Carnival Architects designed the elaborate pavilions and structures for the Manila Carnival (1908–1939), testing Neo-Classical and Art Deco styles. (Source: Architectural Groups (Local), #2 The Manila Carnival Architects)

q: Jørn Utzon (1918–2008), a Danish architect, is renowned for designing which iconic building?
n: Utzon is renowned for designing the iconic Sydney Opera House in Australia, celebrated for its innovative use of sculptural forms. (Source: Famous Architects, #22 Jørn Utzon)

q: Which architect was a Key Collaborator (not a Core Member/Founder) of the Memphis Group?
n: Michael Graves, along with Hans Hollein, Shiro Kuramata, Arata Isozaki, and Peter Shire, was a Key Collaborator of the Memphis Group; the Core Members/Founders included Sottsass, Martine Bedin, Aldo Cibic, Michele De Lucchi, Nathalie Du Pasquier, Matteo Thun, and George J. Sowden. (Source: Architectural Groups (International), #3 The Memphis Group)

q: Peter Eisenman (b. 1932) views architecture as a form of what, and is known for 'deconstructing the grid' in works like the Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe?
n: Eisenman, known for his deconstructivism approach, views architecture as a form of linguistics and is famous for deconstructing the grid, creating complex, fragmented spaces. (Source: Famous Architects, #39 Peter Eisenman)

q: Renzo Piano (b. 1937), an Italian architect celebrated for high-tech and sustainable designs, co-designed which landmark Parisian cultural center?
n: Piano co-designed the Centre Georges Pompidou in Paris, known for its exposed structural elements. (Source: Famous Architects, #44 Renzo Piano)

q: Hector Guimard (1867–1942), a leading figure in the Art Nouveau movement, is best known for his iconic ironwork designs for which structures?
n: Guimard's Paris Métro Entrances (early 1900s), with sinuous cast-iron designs and floral motifs, became synonymous with the Art Nouveau movement. (Source: Famous Architects, #17 Hector Guimard)

q: Sir Christopher Wren (1632–1723), an English architect, astronomer, and mathematician, was instrumental in rebuilding London after which historic event?
n: Wren was instrumental in rebuilding London after the Great Fire of 1666; his works, including St. Paul's Cathedral, are characterized by classical architecture infused with Baroque elements. (Source: Famous Architects, #49 Sir Christopher Wren)

q: Which architect said, "My hand is the extension of the thinking process—the creative process"?
n: "My hand is the extension of the thinking process—the creative process" is a dictum of Tadao Ando (b. 1941). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #17 Tadao Ando)

q: Norman Foster (b. 1935), founder of Foster + Partners, is renowned for sleek, high-tech, and sustainable designs such as which London skyscraper (nicknamed 'The Gherkin')?
n: Foster's notable works include 30 St Mary Axe (The Gherkin), London—a distinctive, energy-efficient skyscraper. (Source: Famous Architects, #35 Norman Foster)

q: The Metabolist Group was officially formed by a younger generation of architects and critics for which 1960 event in Tokyo?
n: The Metabolist Group was officially formed for the 1960 World Design Conference in Tokyo, drafting the manifesto 'Metabolism: The Proposals for a New Urbanism.' (Source: Architectural Groups (International), #2 The Metabolist Group)

q: Frank Lloyd Wright developed which concept—a new interior space idea rejecting rooms as single-function boxes?
n: Wright developed the idea of the Prairie house, rejecting existing views of rooms as single-function boxes and creating overlapping, interpenetrating rooms with shared spaces. (Source: Famous Architects, #14 Frank Lloyd Wright)

q: Which architect said, "Architecture is about understanding the world and turning it into a more meaningful and humane place"?
n: This dictum belongs to Jørn Utzon (1918–2008). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #33 Jørn Utzon)

q: Who was the first pensionado architect, graduating from Drexel Institute in 1908?
n: Carlos Barretto was the first pensionado architect, graduating from Drexel Institute in 1908. (Source: Architectural Groups (Local), #1 The Pensionados)

q: Inigo Jones's Banqueting House (1619) in Whitehall, London holds which distinction?
o: It's the tallest building in England at the time
It's the first Gothic Revival building in England
It's the first building in England designed in a pure classical style
n: The Banqueting House (1619) is the first building in England designed in a pure classical style. (Source: Famous Architects, #20 Inigo Jones)

q: Otto Wagner (1841–1918) was a key figure in which Austrian architectural movement?
n: The Austrian architect and urban planner Wagner was a key figure in the Vienna Secession movement and a pioneer of modern architecture in Austria. (Source: Famous Architects, #36 Otto Wagner)

q: Fumihiko Maki (1928–2024), a founding member of the Metabolist movement, is known for the idea of 'Group Form,' which proposes that buildings should:
o: Be demolished and rebuilt every decade
Be designed as a cluster of parts that can grow and change over time
n: Maki is known for 'Group Form'—the idea that buildings should be designed as a cluster of parts that can grow and change over time, rather than a fixed, singular object. (Source: Famous Architects, #16 Fumihiko Maki)

q: Which architect said, "As an architect, you design for the present, with an awareness of the past, for a future which is essentially unknown"?
n: This dictum belongs to Norman Foster (b. 1935). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #13 Norman Foster)

q: Philip Webb (1831–1915) designed the Red House in Bexleyheath for which fellow Arts and Crafts figure?
n: Webb, a key figure in the Arts and Crafts movement, designed the Red House in Bexleyheath for William Morris; it's considered a seminal Arts and Crafts residence. (Source: Famous Architects, #41 Philip Webb)

q: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe (1886–1969) is known for minimalist designs and coined which famous aphorism?
n: The German-American architect Mies is known for his minimalist designs and the aphorism 'less is more.' (Source: Famous Architects, #30 Ludwig Mies van der Rohe)

q: Pablo S. Antonio (National Artist, 1976) is considered the pioneer of modern Philippine architecture, prioritizing function over ornament and emphasizing:
o: Clean lines, plain surfaces, natural light, and ventilation
Massive concrete structures with long eaves
n: Pablo S. Antonio is considered the pioneer of modern Philippine architecture, with work characterized by clean lines, plain surfaces, and a focus on natural light and ventilation. (Source: National Artist for Architecture, #2 Pablo S. Antonio)

q: Which architect said, "If we learn to build with local materials, we have a future"?
n: This dictum belongs to Francis Kéré (b. 1965). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #42 Francis Kéré)

q: Aldo Rossi's San Cataldo Cemetery in Modena, Italy showcases what approach to architecture?
n: San Cataldo Cemetery in Modena, Italy, showcases Rossi's metaphysical approach to architecture. (Source: Famous Architects, #2 Aldo Rossi)

q: Which of these is a notable work of National Artist Juan F. Nakpil?
n: Nakpil's notable works include Quiapo Church (reconstruction and expansion), UP Administration and Library buildings (Quezon Hall), Capitol Theater Manila, and the Rizal Shrine, Calamba (reconstruction). (Source: National Artist for Architecture, #1 Juan F. Nakpil)

q: Which architect said, "Architects don't invent anything; they transform reality"?
n: "Architects don't invent anything; they transform reality" and "Tradition is a challenge to innovation" are dicta of Alvaro Siza Vieira (b. 1933). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #21 Alvaro Siza Vieira)

q: Which of these is a notable work of Eero Saarinen?
n: Eero Saarinen's notable works include the TWA Flight Center at JFK Airport, the Gateway Arch in St. Louis, and Dulles International Airport. (Source: Famous Architects, #9 Eero Saarinen)

q: Which architect stated, "A Doctor can bury his mistakes, but an architect can only advise his client to plant vines"?
n: This dictum belongs to Frank Lloyd Wright (1867–1959). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #5 Frank Lloyd Wright)

q: Which architect said, "Architecture should speak of its time and place but yearn for timelessness"?
n: This dictum belongs to Frank Gehry (b. 1929). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #27 Frank Gehry)

q: Richard Meier (b. 1934) is associated with 'The New York Five' and is known for what signature design characteristic?
o: Pristine white buildings and geometric designs
n: Meier, associated with 'The New York Five,' is known for his pristine white buildings and geometric designs that emphasize light and space, such as the Getty Center. (Source: Famous Architects, #45 Richard Meier)

q: Which pensionado, known as the most prolific among the group, designed the Manila Central Post Office and the Metropolitan Theater?
n: Juan Arellano, known as the most prolific among the pensionados, designed the Manila Central Post Office and the Metropolitan Theater. (Source: Architectural Groups (Local), #1 The Pensionados)

q: Walter Gropius (1883–1969) was the founder of which influential design school, key to modernist architecture?
n: Gropius, a German architect, was the founder of the Bauhaus School, a key figure in modernist architecture promoting functional design and the integration of art, craft, and technology. (Source: Famous Architects, #52 Walter Gropius)

q: Which architect is famous for the phrase "Less is more"?
n: "Less is more" (and "God is in the details") are famous dicta of Ludwig Mies van der Rohe (1886–1969). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #4 Ludwig Mies van der Rohe)

q: Philip Johnson (1906–2005) was a key figure in introducing modernist architecture to the U.S., and later embraced which subsequent movement?
n: Johnson was a key figure in the introduction of modernist architecture to the U.S. and later embraced postmodernism, as seen in his AT&T Building (now Sony Tower). (Source: Famous Architects, #40 Philip Johnson)

q: The Pensionados were the first Filipino architects sent to the United States as government scholars during which period?
n: The Pensionados were the first Filipino architects sent to the United States as government scholars (pensionados) during the American colonial period, to study Neo-Classical and Beaux-Arts style. (Source: Architectural Groups (Local), #1 The Pensionados)

q: Moshe Safdie (b. 1938) is celebrated for a humanistic approach emphasizing community and livability, exemplified by which revolutionary housing complex?
n: Safdie's Habitat '67 in Montreal is a revolutionary housing complex that reimagined urban living, reflecting his humanistic approach. (Source: Famous Architects, #34 Moshe Safdie)

q: Rem Koolhaas (b. 1944), a Dutch architect and theorist, founded which influential architecture practice?
n: Koolhaas founded the Office for Metropolitan Architecture (OMA) and has influenced contemporary architecture through both practice and theory. (Source: Famous Architects, #43 Rem Koolhaas)

q: Which architect, responding to "Less is more," declared "Yes is more"?
n: "Yes is more" is the well-known dictum of Bjarke Ingels (b. 1974). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #24 Bjarke Ingels)

q: Kisho Kurokawa (1934–2007), a founding member of the Metabolist Movement, is known for the Nakagin Capsule Tower, which emphasized:
o: Flexibility and organic growth in architecture
n: Kurokawa's designs, including the Nakagin Capsule Tower in Tokyo, emphasized flexibility and organic growth in architecture. (Source: Famous Architects, #25 Kisho Kurokawa)

q: The Bauhaus, founded by Walter Gropius in 1919, was led by a group known as the:
n: The Bauhaus school, founded by Walter Gropius in 1919, was led by a 'Council of Masters' who integrated craft, art, and technology. (Source: Architectural Groups (International), #1 The Bauhaus)

q: Marcel Breuer (1902–1981), a Bauhaus protégé, transitioned from furniture design—including the Wassily Chair—to monumental designs in which material and style?
n: Breuer popularized the use of heavy, textured 'beton brut' (raw concrete) and the cantilever in residential architecture, transitioning from furniture design to monumental Brutalism. (Source: Famous Architects, #31 Marcel Breuer)

q: Paul Rudolph (1918–1997), former dean of the Yale School of Architecture, was known for his bold, complex designs and contributions to which movement?
n: Rudolph was known for his bold, complex designs and contributions to the Brutalist movement, as seen in the Yale Art and Architecture Building. (Source: Famous Architects, #37 Paul Rudolph)

q: Which of these is NOT a notable work of Alvar Aalto?
n: Fallingwater is a Frank Lloyd Wright work, not Aalto's. Aalto's notable works include Säynätsalo Town Hall, Paimio Sanatorium, and Villa Mairea. (Source: Famous Architects, #3 Alvar Aalto)

q: Leandro V. Locsin (National Artist, 1990) was nicknamed the 'Poet of Space' for his mastery of geometric forms and massive concrete structures that appear to:
n: Locsin, nicknamed the 'Poet of Space,' mastered heavy materials made to look ethereal—massive concrete that appears to 'float.' (Source: National Artist for Architecture, #3 Leandro V. Locsin)

q: Eliel Saarinen (1873–1950) is recognized for contributions to which architectural style, and later influenced modernist design in the U.S.?
n: Eliel Saarinen is recognized for his contributions to Art Nouveau architecture and later his influence on modernist design in the United States, with notable works like Helsinki Central Railway Station. (Source: Famous Architects, #10 Eliel Saarinen)

q: Which of these is a landscape work of National Artist Ildefonso P. Santos Jr.?
n: Santos's landscape works include the San Miguel Building (Ortigas, Pasig City), Luneta Park (Manila), Tagaytay Highlands (Cavite), and Paco Park (Manila, renovation). (Source: National Artist for Architecture, #4 Ildefonso P. Santos Jr.)

q: 'The New York Five,' also known as 'The Whites,' rose to prominence in the late 1960s and shared an obsession with the pure, white, geometric forms of which early modernist?
n: The New York Five ('The Whites') shared an obsession with the pure, white, geometric forms of early Le Corbusier, and were featured in the 1972 book 'Five Architects.' (Source: Architectural Groups (International), #4 The New York Five)

q: Which architect said, "The straight line belongs to men, the curved one to God"?
n: "The straight line belongs to men, the curved one to God" is a dictum of Antoni Gaudí (1852–1926). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #34 Antoni Gaudí)

q: Hexagon Architects was a collective formed to handle the design and execution of which major Manila structure, and was named for its six prominent members?
o: The National Library of the Philippines
The Cultural Center of the Philippines
n: Hexagon Architects was formed to handle the design and execution of the National Library of the Philippines in Manila, named 'Hexagon' for its six prominent architects. (Source: Architectural Groups (Local), #5 Hexagon Architects)

q: Which pensionado was the first registered architect in the Philippines and founder of Mapua Institute of Technology?
n: Tomas Mapua was the first registered architect in the Philippines and founder of Mapua Institute of Technology. (Source: Architectural Groups (Local), #1 The Pensionados)

q: Which architect was a member of The New York Five who later pivoted to Postmodernism?
n: Michael Graves was a member of The New York Five who later pivoted to Postmodernism; the group also included Peter Eisenman, Charles Gwathmey, John Hejduk, and Richard Meier. (Source: Architectural Groups (International), #4 The New York Five)

q: What is the term for Gaudí's decorative technique using broken mosaic pieces?
n: Trencadís is Gaudí's decorative technique using broken mosaic pieces. (Source: Famous Architects, #4 Antoni Gaudí)

q: Oscar Niemeyer (1907–2012), nicknamed 'the great king of curves,' was a Brazilian architect whose curvaceous modernist designs are integral to the identity of which city?
n: Niemeyer's curvaceous modernist buildings, including the Cathedral of Brasília and the National Congress of Brazil, are integral to the identity of Brasília, Brazil's capital. (Source: Famous Architects, #29 Oscar Niemeyer)

q: Richard Rogers (1933–2021), a pioneer of the high-tech architecture movement, co-designed which building known for having its services exposed on the exterior?
n: Rogers co-designed the Centre Pompidou and is also known for the Lloyd's Building, London, which features services exposed on the exterior. (Source: Famous Architects, #46 Richard Rogers)

q: Ildefonso P. Santos Jr. (National Artist, 2006), popularly known as 'IP Santos,' is regarded as the:
n: Ildefonso P. Santos Jr. is regarded as the 'Father of Philippine Landscape Architecture,' pioneering the practice of landscape architecture in the Philippines. (Source: National Artist for Architecture, #4 Ildefonso P. Santos Jr.)

q: Frank Lloyd Wright (1867–1959) championed which concept of designing structures in harmony with humanity and environment?
n: The iconic American architect Wright championed the concept of 'organic architecture,' designing more than 1,000 structures over his 70-year career. (Source: Famous Architects, #14 Frank Lloyd Wright)

q: The phenomenon of urban revitalization credited to Frank Gehry's titanium-clad Guggenheim Museum Bilbao is known as what?
n: The Guggenheim Museum Bilbao (1997), a titanium-clad museum credited with revitalizing the city, gave rise to the phenomenon termed the 'Bilbao Effect.' (Source: Famous Architects, #13 Frank Gehry)

q: Which architect declared "We are called the architects of the future, not its victims"?
n: "We are called the architects of the future, not its victims" and "Doing more with less" are dicta of Buckminster Fuller (1895–1983). (Source: Famous Architects' Dictum, #8 Buckminster Fuller)

q: Frei Otto (1925–2015) was a pioneer in which type of structural design?
n: The German architect and structural engineer Otto was a pioneer in lightweight and tensile structures, and developed a convertible roof with variable geometry, as seen at the Munich Olympic Stadium (1972). (Source: Famous Architects, #15 Frei Otto)

q: Erich Mendelsohn (1887–1953) was a pioneer of which architectural movement, formulating designs without historical precedents?
n: The German architect Mendelsohn was a pioneer of Expressionist architecture and later contributed to the International Style, using no historical precedents in his designs. His Einstein Tower in Potsdam is a notable example. (Source: Famous Architects, #11 Erich Mendelsohn)

q: Geoffrey Bawa's Heritance Kandalama Hotel, considered one of his greatest masterpieces, is located in which country?
n: The Heritance Kandalama Hotel in Dambulla, Sri Lanka, built into a rocky cliff overlooking the Kandalama Tank and Sigiriya Rock, is considered one of Bawa's greatest masterpieces. (Source: Famous Architects, #8 Deshamanya Geoffrey Bawa)

q: The Memphis Group, founded by Ettore Sottsass in 1980, was a Milan-based design and architecture collective that reacted against what?
n: The Memphis Group, founded by Ettore Sottsass in 1980, reacted against the 'good taste' of Modernism. (Source: Architectural Groups (International), #3 The Memphis Group)

q: Louis Sullivan (1856–1924), an American architect and key figure in the Chicago School, is often referred to as the:
n: Sullivan is often referred to as the 'Father of skyscrapers,' was a key figure in the Chicago School, and was also considered the 'Dean of American Architects.' (Source: Famous Architects, #27 Louis Sullivan)

q: Benjamin Henry Latrobe (1764–1820) is often referred to by which title?
n: The English-born American architect Latrobe is often referred to as the 'father of American architecture' and introduced Greek Revival architecture to the United States. (Source: Famous Architects, #5 Benjamin Henry Latrobe)

q: The Philippine Institute of Architects (PIA), the first professional organization for architects in the country, was founded in what year?
n: The PIA was founded in 1933 as the first professional organization for architects in the Philippines, with founding members including Juan Nakpil, Tomas Mapua, Tomas Arguelles, Andres Luna de San Pedro, and Carlos Barretto. (Source: Architectural Groups (Local), #5 The Philippine Institute of Architects (PIA) Founders)

q: Minoru Yamasaki (1912–1986), an American architect of Japanese descent, is best known for designing which structure?
o: The World Trade Center Twin Towers
n: Yamasaki designed the World Trade Center Twin Towers in New York City, once the tallest buildings in the world and iconic symbols of the city. (Source: Famous Architects, #33 Minoru Yamasaki)

q: Which Austrian firm, led by Wolf Prix and Helmut Swiczinsky, was among the Deconstructivists featured at the 1988 MoMA exhibition?
n: Coop Himmelb(l)au, the Austrian firm led by Wolf Prix and Helmut Swiczinsky, was among the Deconstructivists. (Source: Architectural Groups (International), #5 The Deconstructivists)

q: Louis Sullivan served as a mentor to which other legendary American architect?
n: Sullivan was a mentor to Frank Lloyd Wright. (Source: Famous Architects, #27 Louis Sullivan)
